Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens — Must Read

WSO2 API Manager and related products are under active exploitation for CVE-2026-5430, a critical JWT signature-validation bypass that lets attackers forge administrator tokens and potentially take over accounts. Organizations should immediately apply WSO2’s available fixes and updates.

  • CVE-2026-5430 is a critical WSO2 JWT authentication flaw that allows unauthorized access when tokens are signed with unsupported algorithms but are accepted anyway.
  • watchTowr reported active exploitation attempts, including forged JWT tokens with administrator privileges captured by its honeypot network on September 13, 2026.
  • The affected products include WSO2 API Manager versions 4.1.0 through 4.6.0, along with specified versions of WSO2 API Control Plane, Traffic Manager, and Universal Gateway.
  • WSO2 has released fixes through community pull requests and update levels for WSO2 Support Subscription Holders.
  • According to watchTowr, successful exploitation could expose API backend endpoints, credentials, consumer keys, application secrets, sensitive data in transit, and internal services.

Technologies: api-gateway

Products: wso2-api-manager, wso2-api-control-plane, wso2-traffic-manager, wso2-universal-gateway

Vendors: wso2, watchtowr

Critical ScreenConnect flaw now actively exploited in attacks — Must Read

CISA says attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect authorization flaw that can enable unauthorized file transfer and execution during remote sessions. Organizations should upgrade to ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later immediately, as more than 1,000 exposed instances remain unpatched.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw, to its catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities after attackers began exploiting it in the wild.
  • The missing-authorization and privilege-management flaw can allow attackers with basic privileges to transfer or execute files through active remote sessions without host confirmation.
  • ConnectWise patched the vulnerability in ScreenConnect version 26.6.5 and later, after initially recommending that organizations disable TransferFiles permissions as a temporary mitigation.
  • CISA ordered U.S. federal agencies to secure affected systems within three days because of ongoing attacks.
  • Shadowserver tracked more than 1,000 unpatched ScreenConnect instances exposed online, including 758 in North America and 180 in Europe.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: screenconnect

Vendors: connectwise

Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-27540 in WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture versions through 2.0.3.1 to upload PHP web shells and take over vulnerable WordPress sites. Site owners should update immediately and check for unexpected PHP files, especially in uploads directories.

  • Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-27540, a critical flaw in WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture versions through 2.0.3.1 that allows unauthenticated upload of arbitrary files, including PHP backdoors.
  • Wordfence said it has blocked more than 100,000 exploit attempts targeting the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture flaw since June 2026.
  • Observed attacks submit crafted requests to the wwlc_file_upload_handler action with a forged file_settings parameter and a malicious PHP file named shell.php.
  • The uploaded PHP web shell reports host details and provides a browser-based form for placing additional malicious files on a compromised WordPress site.
  • Wordfence also disclosed two critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw chains affecting The Events Calendar, which StellarWP addressed in versions 6.17.3.1 and 6.17.4.1.

Technologies: cms

Products: woocommerce-wholesale-lead-capture, the-events-calendar, wordpress

Vendors: wordfence, stellarwp, wordpress

Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution — Must Read

A critical Issabel Framework flaw, CVE-2026-89026, is being actively exploited to forge JWTs and remotely execute arbitrary commands as the Asterisk user without authentication. Organizations should apply Issabel’s August 2026 patch immediately.

  • CVE-2026-89026 is a critical Issabel Framework vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary operating system commands.
  • The flaw stems from a hard-coded JWT signing key in the pbxapi index.php file that was identical across Issabel installations.
  • Attackers can forge bearer tokens and invoke the /pbxapi/manager/originate endpoint with Asterisk’s System application parameter to run commands as the Asterisk user.
  • Issabel released a patch on August 1, 2026, replacing the hard-coded JWT key with a key stored in /etc/issabel.conf.
  • Shadowserver Foundation first observed exploitation of the vulnerability on September 9, 2026, and users are advised to apply the latest fixes.

Products: issabel-framework, issabel-pbxapi, asterisk

Vendors: issabel-foundation

Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation — Must Read

Google patched CVE-2026-58704, a high-severity Pixel cellular modem privilege-escalation flaw that may be under limited targeted exploitation. Pixel users should install the September 2026 security update (patch level 2026-09-05 or later) immediately.

  • Google disclosed that CVE-2026-58704 is a high-severity privilege-escalation flaw in the Pixel Cellular Modem with a CVSS score of 8.0.
  • Google said it found indications that CVE-2026-58704 may be under limited, targeted exploitation in the wild.
  • The flaw is caused by a logic error that can permit a nearby attacker to bypass permissions and gain elevated privileges without user interaction.
  • Google's September 2026 Pixel updates address CVE-2026-58704 and 109 other security flaws.
  • Installing a Pixel security patch level of 2026-09-05 or later resolves all of the identified flaws.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: pixel, pixel-cellular-modem, android, android-framework

Vendors: google

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-70756) Oracle WebLogic Server Takeover via T3 and IIOP — Must Read

Oracle WebLogic Server CVE-2026-70756 is a critical pre-authentication flaw (CVSS 9.8) that can allow attackers with network access to T3 or IIOP ports to fully compromise affected servers. Organizations should urgently apply Oracle’s September 2026 CPU patches and restrict external access to T3 and IIOP, especially on TCP ports 7001 and 7002.

  • CVE-2026-70756 is a critical Oracle WebLogic Server flaw with a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8 that can allow an unauthenticated network attacker using T3 or IIOP to take full control of a server.
  • Oracle identifies WebLogic Server versions 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0, 14.1.2.0.0, and 15.1.1.0.0 as affected by CVE-2026-70756.
  • T3 and IIOP can be reachable on WebLogic’s default HTTP listen ports, including TCP ports 7001 and 7002, even when an instance appears externally to be an ordinary web application server.
  • Oracle released fixes for all four affected versions in its September 15, 2026 Critical Security Patch Update.
  • Until patching is confirmed, the article recommends inventorying internet-facing WebLogic systems, restricting T3 and IIOP access, disabling unneeded IIOP, and reviewing load balancer rules that forward full listen ports.

Technologies: web-server

Products: oracle-weblogic-server, oracle-fusion-middleware, cycognito-platform

Vendors: oracle, cycognito

Operation RapidRust: APT36 Deploys RUSTYSHADE, RUSTYMOVE, PSNATCH, and BASHNATCH — Must Read

APT36’s Operation RapidRust targets government and defense organizations in India and Afghanistan with new Rust- and script-based malware that uses private GitHub repositories for encrypted command-and-control and data theft. The campaign also deploys a USB propagation tool to move malware into air-gapped networks and conducts extensive network reconnaissance and lateral-movement activity.

  • In August 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz observed Pakistan-linked APT36 targeting government and defense organizations in India and Afghanistan in a campaign called Operation RapidRust.
  • APT36 used the Rust-based RUSTYSHADE backdoor to communicate through attacker-controlled private GitHub repositories, with command-and-control messages encrypted using AES-256-GCM.
  • The PowerShell-based PSNATCH and Linux-focused BASHNATCH tools scan configured directories for recent files and send collected files to private GitHub repositories.
  • RUSTYMOVE monitors for removable media and copies pre-staged malicious files to external drives, which ThreatLabz assessed could enable spread to air-gapped networks.
  • Observed APT36 activity included system and network discovery, scheduled-task persistence, SMB share access attempts, payload deployment, and deletion of files associated with prior tooling.

Technologies: source-control, cloud-platform, object-storage, operating-system

Products: github, github-rest-api, backblaze-b2, windows, powershell

Vendors: github, backblaze, microsoft, zscaler

Acronis cPanel Backup Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in Targeted Attacks — Must Read

Acronis says a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-87886) in its cPanel/WHM Backup plugin is being exploited in limited targeted attacks. Organizations should immediately update to version 1.9.3 HF3 or later, and update the affected Plesk extension to build 1.8.11.638 or later.

  • Acronis reported that CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity flaw in its Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM, has been exploited in limited targeted attacks.
  • The issue is caused by insecure file permissions and can allow a low-privileged attacker on an affected Linux system to gain higher permissions.
  • The affected Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel and WHM is vulnerable before build 1.9.3.1021, and Acronis fixed it in version 1.9.3 HF3.
  • The Acronis Backup extension for Plesk on Linux is affected before build 1.8.11.638.
  • Acronis advised customers to install the latest updates immediately, while details about the attackers, their goals, and the timing of exploitation remain unavailable.

Technologies: backup

Products: acronis-backup-plugin-for-cpanel-whm, acronis-backup-extension-for-plesk

Vendors: acronis, cpanel, plesk

Malware bypasses browser checks to force install Chrome, Edge extensions — Must Read

KREMLIN banking malware is infecting primarily Brazilian users and covertly installing malicious Chrome and Edge extensions by modifying Chromium profile settings and recreating their integrity checks. The AVSync-branded extensions steal credentials, cookies, session data, keystrokes, screenshots, and web traffic while giving attackers browser-level control.

  • Elastic Security Labs identified KREMLIN, a banking-malware toolkit tied to a Brazilian operation active since mid-2025, which installs malicious Chrome and Edge extensions without user approval.
  • The infection begins when a target opens a JavaScript file disguised as a bank receipt, invoice, payment record, or business document; the file then downloads Node.js, creates a scheduled task, and retrieves payload information from an Ethereum smart contract.
  • KREMLIN copies its extension into browser profile directories, enables developer mode, and modifies Chromium Secure Preferences while regenerating the cryptographic checks needed to make the extension appear valid.
  • The AVSync-branded extension can steal cookies, browser storage, session data, typed form content, screenshots, page source, browsing history, and HTTP request data, and can inject content or redirect clicks.
  • Elastic confirmed 1,515 infected systems, almost all in Brazil, and disrupted the current campaign by registering a domain used by the malware as an anti-sandbox canary.

Technologies: browser, remote-access

Products: google-chrome, microsoft-edge, chromium, node-js, ethereum

Vendors: google, microsoft, elastic, node-js, internet-archive, ethereum

NightEagle targets Russian companies — Should Read

Kaspersky reports that the NightEagle (APT-Q-95) group has expanded from Asian targets to Russian companies, using stolen VPN credentials, the GhostContainer Exchange backdoor, and legitimate tunneling tools to retain access. The group also exploits Active Directory weaknesses and BlueKeep to move laterally, steal credentials, and potentially compromise domain controllers.

  • Kaspersky’s Global Emergency Response Team investigated NightEagle (APT-Q-95) incidents targeting businesses in Russia, expanding beyond the group’s previously reported focus on organizations in Asia.
  • Attackers commonly used compromised valid credentials to access corporate VPNs, with connections originating from Russian IP addresses linked to Cloudflare WARP tunnels and European virtual infrastructure providers.
  • NightEagle deployed the GhostContainer backdoor on Microsoft Exchange servers, using it to process command-and-control instructions, evade security monitoring, and redirect network traffic.
  • The group used Microsoft dev tunnels and rdp2tcp to expose and tunnel Remote Desktop Protocol access, and used Impacket’s atexec utility to create scheduled tasks for port forwarding.
  • In one incident, attackers exploited CVE-2019-0708 (BlueKeep), requested Kerberos tickets with unusual flags, and attempted DCSync activity to obtain domain account password hashes and compromise Active Directory infrastructure.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access, source-control, edr, network-monitoring

Iranian hackers use CHOSEN BRICK Windows malware to spy on targets — Should Read

Iranian state-linked hackers are using CHOSEN BRICK Windows spyware, delivered through WhatsApp and Telegram social-engineering lures, to surveil dissidents, activists, and journalists internationally. The malware steals communications and other data, records audio and screenshots, and can ultimately wipe infected systems.

  • Government agencies warned that Iranian state-linked hackers are using the CHOSEN BRICK Windows malware to target dissidents, activists, and journalists worldwide.
  • The attackers use WhatsApp or Telegram messages that impersonate trusted contacts or technical support agents to persuade victims to open malicious files disguised as legitimate applications.
  • CHOSEN BRICK can collect system information, capture screenshots, record microphone audio, steal email and Telegram or WhatsApp browser data, download additional files, delete files, and wipe an infected computer.
  • The malware establishes persistence through Windows Registry Run keys, adds Microsoft Defender exclusions, and uses a victim-specific Telegram bot for command-and-control communications.
  • The agencies said stolen data is sometimes published on pro-Iranian leak sites, increasing harassment and physical risk for dissidents abroad.

Windows 11 KB5124008 update breaks domain trust for some users — Should Read

Microsoft is investigating reports that Windows 11 KB5124008 can break Active Directory domain trust on some enterprise devices after reboot, preventing valid domain logins. Administrators suspect the Machine Identity Isolation/Credential Guard setting is involved, but Microsoft has not issued an official workaround.

  • Microsoft is investigating reports that the Windows 11 KB5124008 security update breaks Active Directory domain trust relationships on some enterprise systems after reboot.
  • Affected users may be unable to log in with valid domain credentials, while cached credentials can continue working when systems are offline.
  • Administrators reported that uninstalling KB5124008 and repairing the computer’s secure channel restored access, but reinstalling the update caused the problem to return.
  • Reports link the failures to the Machine Identity Isolation setting, particularly when it is enabled in audit or enforcement mode.
  • Microsoft has not confirmed the root cause or published an official workaround.

Vendors: microsoft

GitHub Actions Adds cache-mode to Limit Cache Poisoning Risk — Should Read

GitHub Actions introduced cache-mode to restrict cache reads and writes per workflow or job, reducing the risk that untrusted workflows poison caches later used by privileged builds. The feature adds read, write, write-only, and none modes, but does not mitigate other risks from running untrusted code or scripts in CI.

  • GitHub added cache-mode to GitHub Actions to control cache access at the workflow or job level and reduce cache-poisoning risk.
  • Cache poisoning can allow an attacker to place malicious build artifacts or dependencies in a shared Actions cache that a trusted workflow later restores and runs.
  • cache-mode supports read, write, write-only, and none settings, with job-level settings overriding workflow-level settings.
  • GitHub recommends cache-mode: none for AI agent workflows that process untrusted issue or pull-request text.
  • The feature does not address other GitHub Actions risks, including checking out untrusted code, running package lifecycle scripts, or minting OIDC tokens in a runner.

Products: github-actions, github-actions-cache, pypi, npm, cline-cli

Coast Guard, FBI boarded tanker after attack by ‘foreign cyber actors’ — Should Read

The U.S. Coast Guard and FBI boarded a tanker in the Gulf of Mexico after its network was reportedly compromised by foreign cyber actors, though officials said there were no operational or environmental impacts. The incident is part of reports that at least two U.S.-bound tankers were targeted.

  • The U.S. Coast Guard said it boarded a tanker transiting the Gulf of Mexico in August after indications that foreign cyber actors had compromised the vessel’s network.
  • On August 21, a team including Coast Guard law enforcement, cyber personnel, a vessel inspector, and FBI Cyber Action Team operators conducted a cybersecurity investigation aboard the vessel.
  • The Coast Guard said there were no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, crew danger, or environmental impacts from the incident.
  • Reports identified one potentially affected vessel as VL Prosperity, a Liberian-flagged tanker traveling from Egypt to the United States that reportedly lost communications for 30 hours after an August 7 incident near the Strait of Gibraltar.
  • The Wall Street Journal reported that at least two U.S.-bound tankers were targeted and that another vessel was boarded on August 24.

One Extension Could Hijack AI Assistants Across Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon and Claude — Should Read

Researchers found that a malicious browser extension with common permissions could hijack built-in AI assistants in Chrome, Comet, Edge, Opera Neon, and Claude in Chrome, potentially enabling actions such as file access, screenshots, and agent control. The attacks require the victim to install the extension first; Chrome and Edge have issued fixes, while users should update all affected browsers and review installed extensions.

  • Forever Security demonstrated that a browser extension with two common permissions could hijack built-in AI assistants in Chrome, Perplexity Comet, Microsoft Edge, Opera Neon, and Claude in Chrome.
  • The demonstrations required an attacker-controlled extension to already be installed in the victim's browser, and the article reported no evidence that the methods had been used in real attacks.
  • The Chrome method, tracked as CVE-2026-0628, could read local files, take screenshots, and enable the camera and microphone, and Google fixed it in Chrome version 143.0.7499.192.
  • The Edge issue, tracked as CVE-2026-55945, was fixed in Edge version 150.0.4078.48, while the Comet, Opera Neon, and Claude in Chrome findings had no CVE listed.
  • Researchers described Comet as the broadest-impact case because its AI agent could read files, list visited sites, take screenshots, and act as the user after being hijacked.

Technologies: browser

Products: google-chrome, gemini-live, perplexity-comet, microsoft-edge, opera-neon, claude-in-chrome

Vendors: forever-security, google, perplexity, microsoft, opera, anthropic

Attacker Hijacks AI Coding Assistant Session, Spreads Shai-Hulud Across About 100 Repositories — Should Read

Mandiant reported that an attacker hijacked an active AI coding-assistant session, used a poisoned PyPI recommendation to steal secrets and GitHub OAuth tokens, then spread the Shai-Hulud worm across about 100 internal repositories. The incident highlights the need to verify AI-suggested dependencies, restrict extension access to credentials, and use controlled package repositories.

  • Mandiant reported that an attacker hijacked an active AI coding-assistant session at an unnamed software-as-a-service provider and later spread the Shai-Hulud worm across approximately 100 internal repositories.
  • The attacker used a developer’s active session to install an information-stealing program through a poisoned PyPI package and stole GitHub OAuth tokens.
  • The Shai-Hulud worm stole repository secrets and source code for the company’s products.
  • The attacker poisoned a package in the company’s official namespace, and another employee downloaded the compromised version, causing a second infection.
  • Mandiant recommends validating AI-recommended dependencies with cryptographic checksums and approved allowlists, keeping long-lived credentials out of extension reach, and routing dependency traffic through controlled internal repositories.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry

Products: github, pypi, npm, claude-code, visual-studio-code

Vendors: mandiant, github, pypi, npm, anthropic, microsoft

Spain's data agency gets first report of AI-powered data breach — Should Read

Spain’s data protection agency has received its first report of a data breach allegedly conducted by an autonomous AI agent that found vulnerabilities, accessed systems, altered personal data, and viewed financial documents. The report is unverified but underscores that AI can dramatically increase the speed and scale of cyberattacks.

  • The Spanish Data Protection Agency received a report of an alleged data breach carried out using an AI agent powered by a known large language model.
  • According to the reporting organization, the AI agent searched for flaws, logged into systems, found additional application weaknesses, modified personal data, and accessed invoices.
  • The AEPD has not yet investigated or verified the report, but said it demonstrates that AI-related data breaches are no longer only theoretical.
  • The agency said AI does not create new threats but can increase the speed, scale, and adaptability of cyberattacks while reducing the time available for defenders to respond.
  • The AEPD urged organizations to review their security and data-protection models, strengthen credential security, and use rapid detection, containment, and response mechanisms.

Parallels Desktop Flaw Lets Non-Admin Mac Users Gain Root, but Intel Macs Can't Install Fix — Should Read

A local privilege-escalation flaw in Parallels Desktop 26 can let any non-admin Mac user gain root through argument injection in the appliance-install service. JFrog says Parallels Desktop 27 fixes it, but Intel Macs cannot install that version and currently lack a confirmed patched release.

  • JFrog disclosed CVE-2026-90894, nicknamed ParaShells, a flaw in Parallels Desktop that can let a non-administrator local Mac account run code as root.
  • The issue stems from a world-writable Parallels service socket and appliance-install command construction that can allow a folder name containing a quote to inject extra tar options.
  • JFrog demonstrated the flaw on Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 on an Apple silicon Mac and said no virtual machine needs to be running for the attack.
  • JFrog identifies Parallels Desktop 27.0.0 as the fixed version, while the newest 27.0.1 build is available only for Apple silicon Macs running macOS Sonoma 14.7 or newer.
  • Intel Mac users must remain on the Parallels Desktop 26 line, and JFrog says 26.x, including 26.4.2, does not contain the identified extract-command change.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system

Products: parallels-desktop-26, parallels-desktop-27, macos

Vendors: parallels, jfrog, apple

Atomic macOS (AMOS) Stealer Activity — Should Read

Atomic macOS (AMOS) stealer is an actively evolving macOS infostealer spread through malicious software-installation pages that trick users into pasting commands into Terminal. It establishes persistence, requests access to user data and applications, and exfiltrates credentials, browser data, messaging data, cryptocurrency-wallet information, and other files to changing command-and-control infrastructure.

  • The article analyzes an Atomic macOS (AMOS) stealer infection generated in a lab on August 5, 2026, after a user followed instructions on a malicious website advertising a “macOS toolkit.”
  • The malicious page at getmacouscloud[.]com instructed users to copy and paste text into Terminal, which downloaded a Zsh script and ultimately installed AMOS stealer components.
  • The infection saved persistent files under hidden-looking directories in the user’s Library/Application Support folder, including AccountsHelper and mdworker_shared Mach-O binaries.
  • After the user entered an administrative password, Terminal requested access to Finder, the Desktop and Documents folders, and the Notes application.
  • AMOS collected data into /tmp/out.zip and sent HTTP POST requests to a command-and-control server, with URL paths indicating collection of messengers, credentials, browsers, wallets, and local data.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: macos, terminal, zsh

Vendors: apple, palo-alto-networks

TrustSink: How a Rogue External MFA Provider Steals Passwords — May Read

Varonis researchers demonstrated TrustSink, a post-compromise technique in which a privileged attacker registers a rogue Microsoft Entra External Authentication Method that mimics a Microsoft password prompt, captures plaintext passwords, and returns valid signed tokens to complete MFA sign-ins. Defenders should monitor Entra authentication-policy and application changes, remove suspicious providers before resetting passwords, and restrict privileged identity roles.

  • Varonis Threat Labs demonstrated TrustSink, a technique that uses a rogue Microsoft Entra External Authentication Method to present a fake password page during a legitimate sign-in flow and capture plaintext passwords.
  • An attacker needs a Global Administrator or Authentication Policy Administrator account to register the rogue provider, making TrustSink a post-compromise technique.
  • The rogue provider can return a valid signed token to Entra after collecting a password, allowing the victim's sign-in to complete normally without an error.
  • Resetting a captured password alone does not remove the rogue provider, which can capture the replacement password at the user’s next sign-in.
  • Defenders should watch for unauthorized Authentication Methods Policy changes, suspicious application and service-principal registrations, unfamiliar sign-in issuers reporting hardware-key claims, and scripted Microsoft Graph activity.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-entra, microsoft-graph, azure-cli, azure-powershell, ngrok, fastapi

Vendors: microsoft, varonis, ngrok, fastapi

House passes bill to equip local law enforcement with scam-fighting tools — May Read

The U.S. House passed the bipartisan GUARD Act, allowing local law enforcement to use existing DOJ grant funds for financial-fraud investigations, training, and blockchain tracing tools. The bill aims to improve responses to scams, particularly cryptocurrency fraud targeting older Americans.

  • The U.S. House passed the bipartisan GUARD Act, which would allow local law enforcement to use existing federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud.
  • The bill would permit spending on fraud analysts, victim-assistance training, investigative software, financial-institution contacts, and blockchain tracing tools for stolen cryptocurrency.
  • The legislation addresses complaints that local police often lack the resources and tools to investigate online scams that do not receive federal investigation.
  • Americans lost a record $11.4 billion to cryptocurrency-related fraud in 2025, including $8.6 billion from investment fraud.
  • The House also passed a separate bill that would remove taxes on money stolen through scams and apply retroactively to victims scammed from 2021 through 2025.

Three Ukrainians to face charges for alleged hack of 610,000 Roblox accounts — May Read

Ukrainian prosecutors charged three suspects over the alleged theft and resale of access to more than 610,000 Roblox accounts, using stolen session tokens and information-stealing malware. The operation allegedly targeted accounts with valuable virtual assets and may have generated about $480,000 in sales.

  • Ukrainian prosecutors said three suspects will face trial over the alleged theft and resale of access to more than 610,000 Roblox accounts between May 2025 and April 2026.
  • Authorities said the group distributed information-stealing malware disguised as software offering gaming advantages or free in-game bonuses.
  • Investigators said the suspects used stolen session tokens to access accounts and identify those containing valuable virtual currency, rare items, or other digital assets.
  • The group allegedly advertised stolen accounts through Russian online platforms, received cryptocurrency payments, and could have generated roughly $480,000 from sales.
  • All three suspects are in custody and face charges including theft, money laundering, unauthorized interference with computer systems, and illegal sale of restricted information.

Products: roblox

Vendors: roblox

Flock camera use by internal affairs unit puts DC police at odds with officers’ union — May Read

Washington, D.C.’s police union is challenging the Metropolitan Police Department’s use of Flock license-plate-reader cameras to track officers under internal-affairs investigation, citing inadequate oversight and transparency. The dispute, headed to arbitration, reflects widening backlash against Flock’s surveillance technology and has prompted DC Council scrutiny.

  • Washington, D.C.’s Metropolitan Police Department used Flock automated license-plate-reader cameras to track sworn officers under internal-affairs investigation, according to the DC Police Union.
  • The DC Police Union filed a complaint seeking to stop the tracking, but said management denied it and declined to investigate managers involved in the searches.
  • MPD said its position is that using license-plate-reader data in the misconduct investigation was appropriate, and that its dispute with the union is headed to arbitration.
  • The union said MPD issued a new teletype restricting department-wide access to the system on the same day the grievance was denied, while MPD declined to comment on the alleged restrictions or their timing.
  • DC Councilmember Brooke Pinto asked MPD Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll for answers about how the department uses Flock data and why it needs the technology.

EU chief wants joint response to cyberattacks, sabotage — May Read

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed an EU Emergency Security Protocol that would let any member state convene all 27 governments to coordinate responses to sabotage, cyberattacks and drone incursions. The proposal aims to address escalating hybrid threats, though its powers and interaction with the EU’s unanimity-based decision-making rules remain unclear.

  • European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed an Emergency Security Protocol that would allow a single EU member state to convene all 27 governments over threats including sabotage, cyberattacks, and drone incursions.
  • Von der Leyen cited recent incidents in Denmark, Lithuania, and Poland, as well as an attempted drone attack in Leipzig, as evidence that threats were mounting in Europe.
  • The proposed protocol is modeled on NATO’s Article 4 consultation process, but the proposal did not explain what action would follow once governments convene.
  • Many EU foreign and security-policy decisions, including sanctions, require unanimous agreement, and Von der Leyen did not say whether the protocol would change those rules.
  • The Commission also plans a European security strategy that would include a European Security Council and an instrument supporting air and missile defense, strategic transport, refuelling, space, and cyber capabilities.

Ukraine moves to crack down on scam call centers after corruption scandal — May Read

Ukraine’s parliament passed legislation imposing up to 12 years in prison for operating, staffing, or recruiting for scam call centers, following allegations that Prosecutor General’s Office officials accepted bribes to protect such operations. The measure awaits President Zelenskyy’s signature amid broader law-enforcement crackdowns on fraud centers targeting victims in Ukraine and abroad.

  • Ukraine’s parliament approved legislation that creates separate criminal offenses for using electronic communications to commit fraud and for establishing, running, working at, or recruiting people for fraudulent call centers.
  • People convicted of organizing or working for fraudulent call centers could face seven to 12 years in prison under the legislation, which awaits President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s signature.
  • The legislation was advanced after anti-corruption agencies investigated allegations that Prosecutor General’s Office officials accepted bribes from scam call centers in exchange for protection from law enforcement.
  • Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau said five people were named as suspects, while former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko denied protecting scam centers and has not been charged.
  • Ukrainian authorities said they shut down 94 suspected fraudulent call centers during a nationwide operation involving 411 searches.

Windows Server 2022 reaches end of mainstream support next month — May Read

Windows Server 2022 leaves mainstream support on October 13, 2026, after which it will receive free monthly security updates under extended support through October 14, 2031. Microsoft recommends administrators plan a migration to Windows Server 2025 before then.

  • Windows Server 2022 will reach the end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026, with the October 2026 security update being its last mainstream-support update.
  • Windows Server 2022 will enter extended support after October 13, 2026 and continue receiving monthly security updates at no additional cost through October 14, 2031.
  • Hotpatching for Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition has been extended through October 2027.
  • Microsoft recommends that administrators plan to upgrade to Windows Server 2025 and begin deployment testing early.
  • Windows Server 2025 will reach the end of mainstream support on November 13, 2029 and extended support on November 14, 2034.

Products: windows-server-2022, windows-server-2025, windows-10, datacenter-azure-edition

The Fake IRS Notice That Disproved Itself — May Read

A phishing email impersonating the IRS exposed itself through an impossible CP2000 tax-year claim: it referenced a return that could not yet have been filed or reconciled. The case shows that checking internal inconsistencies in authoritative-looking messages can identify fraud before analyzing links or headers.

  • The phishing email impersonated the IRS and contained conflicting claims about a “2026 filing year” and a “CP2000 Notice - Tax Year 2026.”
  • A CP2000 notice compares a filed tax return with third-party reporting, so the article states that it cannot exist before the return for the named tax year has been filed.
  • The message used the display name “IRS.GOV” on an unrelated sending domain and placed the real recipient only in the envelope and delivery header.
  • The email’s single download button linked to imahdyirs.es, which was behind a shared CDN proxy and returned a 403 response to the scanner.
  • IRONSCALES quarantined the message roughly seven seconds after receipt based on its malicious-link verdict, language and structure analysis, and community resolutions of similar incidents.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis

International Meteor Organization says cyberattack dealt ‘critical blow’ to website — May Read

The International Meteor Organization said a cyberattack severely damaged its aging website infrastructure, forcing much of the site offline for weeks while it migrates to new services. Its fireball reporting system has been restored, and no group has claimed responsibility.

  • The International Meteor Organization said a cyberattack dealt a critical blow to its aging infrastructure and took much of its website offline.
  • The organization expects several weeks of partial downtime while it transitions to new infrastructure and services.
  • The IMO prioritized restoring its fireball reporting system, which is available for user submissions.
  • No hacking group had claimed responsibility for the incident as of Wednesday afternoon.
  • The Belgium-based organization maintains meteor and fireball reports, including photos, videos, and telescopic data, and is scheduled to hold its annual conference in France the following week.

Microsoft is still investigating a Classic Outlook for Windows bug that can make Copilot and Copilot Chat buttons disappear after build 20026.20182. A temporary workaround is to enable “Show Apps in Outlook,” while creating a new profile or using Outlook on the web also avoids the issue.

  • Microsoft is still investigating an issue that causes Copilot and Copilot Chat buttons to disappear in Classic Outlook for Windows after upgrading to build 20026.20182 or later.
  • The issue affects users with Copilot Chat (Basic) licenses or paid Microsoft 365 Copilot accounts and can remove Copilot from the ribbon, navigation bar, and app-launch options.
  • Microsoft said its current analysis indicates that affected Outlook installations cannot locate a required profile email-address setting, preventing Copilot-related settings from being saved.
  • Microsoft’s temporary workaround is to enable the “Show Apps in Outlook” option under File, Options, Advanced, and Outlook panes.
  • Users can also create a new Outlook profile or use the new Outlook client or Outlook on the web, which Microsoft says are not affected by this issue.

The N0va phishing kit targets North American and European organizations by impersonating trusted business platforms and abusing legitimate device-code authentication flows to steal tokens and gain SSO access to corporate resources. Securing the unpatchable in an age of AI-driven vulnerabilities — Optional

As AI accelerates discovery of flaws in legacy, unpatchable OT systems, organizations should compensate with asset visibility, strict micro-segmentation, and upstream next-generation firewall/IPS controls. Air gaps can help but are often undermined by operational shortcuts and should not be treated as absolute protection.

  • AI-assisted code analysis is increasing the discovery of vulnerabilities, creating a difficult patching cadence for organizations and increasing risk for unsupported or unpatchable systems.
  • Operational technology systems, including medical equipment, building management systems, and industrial systems in chemical plants, may be unable to apply patches because they are certified for fixed software or use unsupported platforms.
  • Organizations can use asset visibility and network micro-segmentation with VLANs and access control lists to restrict vulnerable OT systems to authorized connections.
  • Next-generation firewalls with up-to-date intrusion prevention systems can inspect incoming traffic and block known exploit attempts before they reach a vulnerable device.
  • Air gaps and one-way data-transfer devices can be undermined when staff or contractors introduce temporary connections or shortcuts that become permanent.

Post-quantum cryptography migration is not just a cryptographic upgrade: organizations need network visibility to identify negotiated protocols, certificates, and dependencies before quantum-safe changes can be deployed safely.

How to Mitigate the Lethal Trifecta That Infects 98% of Agents — Optional

AI agents become highly vulnerable to prompt-injection-driven data theft when they combine access to sensitive data, untrusted content, and outbound actions. Reduce the risk by separating these capabilities across agents and enforcing least privilege, content inspection, DLP, and action controls.

  • The article describes the AI-agent “lethal trifecta” as the combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate or act externally.
  • When an agent has all three capabilities, malicious instructions in untrusted content can trick it into accessing private data and sending it to an attacker.
  • The article distinguishes prompt injection, which attacks applications built on language models, from jailbreaking, which attempts to bypass protections built into the models themselves.
  • The article recommends designing automation as multiple agents, such as separating a document-reading agent from an action-taking agent that does not directly receive untrusted content.
  • For agents that cannot immediately be redesigned, the article recommends discovering agent capabilities, inspecting incoming content, enforcing least-privilege access and data-loss controls, governing agent actions, and analyzing prompts and responses for malicious instructions.

As AI coding agents become widely used by non-technical employees, running them in managed cloud environments can provide stronger centralized access controls, network egress restrictions, sandboxing, and governance than endpoint execution. Organizations must still address cloud compute costs, container-escape risk, and data-residency requirements.

  • The article argues that when non-technical employees use code-capable agents, they may inadvertently expose credentials, publish internal data, or reach data environments they are not authorized to access.
  • Running agents in managed cloud environments can make it easier to centrally control data access, network connections, software updates, and organizational policies.

Acronis warns of actively exploited flaw in its cPanel backup plugin — Should Read

Acronis warns that CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw in its cPanel/WHM and Plesk backup integrations, has been exploited in limited targeted attacks. Administrators should immediately update to Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM 1.9.3 HF3 or Acronis Backup extension for Plesk 1.8.11.

  • Acronis disclosed CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity local privilege-escalation flaw affecting its backup integrations for cPanel & WHM and Plesk on Linux servers.
  • Acronis says it detected exploitation of the flaw in limited, targeted attacks, based on one report from a potentially affected customer.
  • A low-privileged attacker could use the flaw to gain greater permissions on a vulnerable Linux server, potentially accessing or modifying sensitive data or disrupting the system.
  • The affected Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM versions earlier than 1.9.3.1021 are fixed in version 1.9.3 HF3, while affected Plesk extension versions earlier than 1.8.11.638 are fixed in version 1.8.11.
  • Acronis has not released technical details or specific indicators of compromise and recommends that affected users apply the available updates immediately.

A compromise of the Admin Menu Editor Pro update server distributed trojanized versions 2.35 and 2.36, installing web shells and hidden WordPress users on potentially more than 1,500 sites. Customers should restore from a known-safe backup or remove the malicious plugin files, object-cache directory, and associated database entries.

KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens — Should Read

Elastic researchers uncovered KREMLIN, a Brazilian banking-malware operation that installs malicious Chrome and Edge extensions to steal credentials, session tokens, cookies, and browser data. The campaign uses multi-stage loaders, SentinelOne DLL sideloading, Chromium preference-integrity bypasses, and Ethereum smart contracts to rotate its command-and-control infrastructure.

  • Elastic Security Labs identified a Brazilian banking-malware operation tracked as REF9334 that has been active since at least May 2025 and delivers a toolkit called KREMLIN.

  • KREMLIN bypasses Chromium extension protections by modifying Secure Preferences, enabling developer mode, and generating forged metadata to register its malicious extension.

Censys identified 131 internet-exposed Mythic C2 hosts, most recognizable through default TLS certificates and port 7443 behavior. While some deployments appear to be labs, others show sophisticated operational infrastructure, making these fingerprints useful for proactive network and host-based detection.

  • Mythic is an open-source, plugin-based command-and-control framework used in authorized security testing and observed in unauthorized intrusions.
  • As of September 11, 2026, Censys tracked 131 unique publicly exposed hosts matching Mythic detections, with 115 presenting certificates whose subject organization was "Mythic" or "Mythic C2."
  • Port 7443 appeared on 99 tracked hosts, and Mythic's default Nginx reverse proxy returns an HTTP 502 response to unauthenticated requests on that port.
  • Ten of the 131 tracked hosts also exposed at least one additional command-and-control framework, including Sliver, Adaptix C2, Havoc, or FRP.
  • Censys recommends that defenders monitor for Mythic default certificate names, the CN=operators to CN=multiplayer certificate chain, and unexpected Mythic Docker container names.
